title: export-http-metadata-and-tool-context-for-endpoint-affinity-telemetry
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Add HTTP metadata exporter and tool-call context fields to structured API logs and metrics; allow per-endpoint affinity tagging for telemetry aggregation; backward-compatible opt-in via feature flag
description:
Summary: Exports richer HTTP metadata and tool-call context to the API observable surface. Adds endpoint-affinity tags that let downstream metrics (Prom/Tempo/JSONL logs) group by logical endpoint affinity and tool execution context. This change is targeted at improving root-cause analysis for transient streaming instability and function/tool-calling errors, and to make cost/latency aggregation more accurate per logical route.

Motivation and background: We often lose useful HTTP-level metadata (user-agent variants, negotiated protocol, upstream proxy id) and tool execution context (tool id, tool-args-hash, tool-runtime) in our structured logs and metrics. That gap makes incident triage slow when streaming fragments fail mid-flight or when tool-bound calls cause tail latency. This PR adds a compact exporter that augments the request envelope used by the API surface and the OpenAI-compat shim so observability outputs (jsonl access logs, metrics dimensions, and tracing spans) include: http.metadata.* and tool.context.* fields. The change is designed to be low-overhead and opt-in via the existing telemetry.feature_flags map (default: off for private installs).

What I changed (high level):
- Introduced http_metadata_exporter module that extracts and canonicalizes HTTP headers we care about and attaches them to the request context for downstream telemetry.
- Added tool_call_context enrichment: when a function/tool call is invoked we attach small, stable identifiers (tool.id, tool.version, tool.arg_hash) to the active span and to structured logs.
- Endpoint affinity: added a per-route affinity tag (route.affinity_id) computed from route config to group metrics/alerts by logical endpoint (useful for multi-compat adapter routes).
- Plumbed the enrichment through the OpenAI-compat adapter so both native Redwood API and OpenAI-compatible endpoints export the same fields.
- Tests: unit tests for canonicalization logic, integration tests exercising streaming with tool calls, and a perf test ensuring <1% p99 tail increase for typical workloads.

Backward compatibility and performance: The enrichment is behind telemetry.feature_flags.http_metadata_export (default off for on-prem/private). Hosted customers are enabled by default and rolled out with a gradual ramp via config. Exported fields are small strings or short tags and only attached when enabled; we validated with perf-regression runs that p50/p95 are unchanged and p99 increased by <1% at the stress levels used in our perf lab.

Testing and CI summary: CI initially failed on e2e streaming due to a missed context copy in the stream-to-worker handoff. Fixed in commit 6f7g8h9. Final CI: all checks pass. Perf artifacts uploaded to the benchmark lab (link: internal/bench/telemetry/75618). Integration test exercise matrix included: http/1.1 vs http/2 streaming, proxied vs direct, tool-call success/failure paths.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag gated (telemetry.feature_flags.http_metadata_export).
- Canary on dedicated infra for 48h (10% traffic) with new metrics dashboards showing route.affinity groupings and tool-context slicers.
- Full rollout to hosted after canary validation; on-prem remains opt-in via chart values.

Review conversation (high level):
- Diego Montoya (reviewer) - 2026-02-19: "Can we avoid adding entire headers into logs? prefer whitelist + normalization. Also please confirm we don't leak PII (x-forwarded-for truncation)."
- Asha (author) - 2026-02-19: "Implemented header whitelist + normalization; x-forwarded-for now uses last-n IPs and masks the final octet for IPv4; added tests."
- Priya Rao (reviewer) - 2026-02-20: "Need clearer metric labels for route.affinity to avoid high-cardinality explosion. Suggest combinatorial guard and a max-cardinality limiter."
- Asha - 2026-02-20: "Added cardinality guard in route_affinity.rs and a config knob route.affinity.max_tags (default 50). Unit tests added."
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer) - 2026-02-22: "Integration tests look good; one flake on streaming handoff reported."
- Asha - 2026-02-24: "Fixed streaming handoff and added an integration test covering the case. CI green."
- Diego - 2026-02-25: "LGTM, approving. Please squash-merge after perf artifacts are linked."

Merge and post-merge actions: Squash-merged into main with commit a3f9b2c4d7e1. Updated release_notes and added docs in docs/observability/http-metadata.md. Created dashboard PR in observability-pack to add a route-affinity panel and tool-context slicer (follow-up: pr-76002).

Notes for on-call and SRE: If you see sudden high-cardinality spikes on metric route.affinity.*, toggle telemetry.feature_flags.http_metadata_export=false to stop enrichment while we triage (this reverts only the enrichment, not core request handling). There is a short playbook entry in docs/observability/http-metadata.md under "Operational toggles".

Related work: ENG-4981 (observability data model cleanup), ENG-5012 (tool-call reliability), SUP-908 (customer case where streaming failure lacked tool context).

summary_line: Add opt-in HTTP metadata and tool-call context enrichment to API observability with per-route affinity tagging (flag-gated; canary + opt-in).
